- When sentiment is negative and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a recent dip, cap the overshoot at +10% above the 14-day moving average.  
- When sentiment is positive and forecast is trending downward, adjust downward by 3–5% to avoid premature sell-off.  
- For 30-day forecasts, apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is >15% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, align forecast with 14-day moving average rather than 30-day trend.  
- Avoid forecasting below 50% of recent 18-day low unless sentiment is strongly bearish and confirmed by 3 consecutive negative sentiment days.
